statement: Among 1200-1600 players, a 2+ game winning streak is followed by outperformance vs their other games
rationale: Momentum or confidence and in-form play may raise performance beyond rating, especially in mid-level players whose ratings lag form.

statement: Among 1600-2000 players, the first game of a session underperforms their other games
rationale: Warm-up effects: players are cold at session start and play below their typical strength.

statement: Among 2000-2400 players, being Black in 3+0 games underperforms more than average
rationale: White advantage is amplified in fast bullet-like blitz where initiative matters and strong players convert it.

statement: Games after a loss with a long break (60+ min) rebound relative to the player's other games
rationale: A cooling-off period after a loss should remove tilt, so players return fresh.

statement: Among <1200 players, playing 10+ games in a day (fatigue) lowers performance vs their other games
rationale: Fatigue and frustration accumulate in beginners across many games.

statement: Games played against 2400+ opponents by 2000-2400 players outperform Elo expectation modestly less
rationale: Elo compression/inflation among top players may make underdogs perform below expectation versus elite opposition.

statement: In arenas, players with a losing streak of 2+ underperform relative to their other games
rationale: Arena tilt: losing in tournaments produces chasing and rushed play, plus pairing with strong opponents.

statement: Among 1200-1600 players, games in 5+0 as Black after a loss underperform
rationale: Tilt and colour disadvantage compound; negative emotion after a loss hurts more with the harder colour.

statement: Weekday evening games (18-22 UTC) on Fri outperform the player's other games
rationale: Relaxed leisure play at the weekend start may differ from usual play; no strong prior on direction.

statement: Among 1600-2000 players, 3+2 games with increment outperform 3+0 vs their other games
rationale: Increment reduces flagging and could change who benefits; ratings are pooled across controls so residuals may differ.

statement: Among 1200-1600 players, D-family openings (queen's pawn) outperform their other games
rationale: Solid d4 openings are more theory-based; players who choose them tend to play structured chess, getting more reliable results.

statement: Among 2000-2400 players, A-family flank openings underperform
rationale: Offbeat openings may be less accurate against well-prepared opposition at high level.

statement: Rapid replays after a draw (<=3 minutes since previous start) differ from the player's other games
rationale: Quick draws may reflect agreed short games; effect on the next game is unclear.

statement: Among 1600-2000 players, previous abandoned or time-forfeit wins lead to overconfidence
rationale: Winning on time may indicate lucky wins in lost positions, leaving the player with false confidence.

statement: Late-night (UTC 22-23) games among 1200-1600 players differ from daytime
rationale: Late evening fatigue and alcohol/tiredness may lower play quality.

statement: Among 2400+ players, favourites facing a lower-rated opponent (-diff 100+) in a session beyond game 10 underperform
rationale: Elite players on long sessions may grind low-rated opponents carelessly or with premoves, risking upsets.

statement: Winning streak of 1 combined with a quick next game (<=5 min) in 1600-2000 band outperforms
rationale: Flow state: players continuing quickly while winning stay engaged and perform well.

statement: Second game of a session after a loss underperforms among <1200 players
rationale: Immediate frustration from an opening loss leads to poorer follow-up play among beginners.

statement: Sunday games in 1200-1600 band as White outperform
rationale: Weekend casual play may weaken the opposition's quality relative to ratings; no strong prior.
